name: Financial-sector end-to-end workforce identity and access controls

attribution.legal_posture: Official risk-based guidance for regulated financial-services entities; it supplies guidance rather than a named incident, adjudication, or universal mandatory checklist.

caveats: Risk-based guidance with documented review; nationality profiling is outside the method.
This record includes no people, personas, victim institutions, front companies, accounts, wallets, payment identifiers, addresses, or images.
Treat controls as risk-based and source-qualified; DPRK linkage requires multiple corroborated signals.

statements: NYDFS connects hiring, third-party staffing, device custody, network monitoring, least privilege, and incident reporting in one DPRK-specific advisory for regulated entities. The strongest unique contribution is organizational: HR, security, IT, senior executives, and service providers are expected to coordinate rather than treat applicant screening as a one-time HR check.
limitations: Present as risk-based guidance, not a mandatory universal checklist or a basis for nationality profiling.
Treat controls as risk-based and source-qualified; no single location, language, accent, camera, payment, network, device, or behavioral signal establishes DPRK linkage.
This record includes no people, personas, victim institutions, front companies, accounts, wallets, payment identifiers, addresses, or images.

sources.support: DFS describes false or stolen identities, U.S.-based proxy participants, alternate device-delivery locations, remote-access software, and native-tool use. It recommends cross-functional awareness, staffing-platform and staffing-agency diligence, layered identity and reference checks, proxy detection, asset geolocation, review of address changes and atypical work patterns, restriction of remote-access tools, least privilege with gradual access expansion, enhanced monitoring, and regulatory/law-enforcement reporting.
